answers.ninjo: Seka wants to be asked before someone else decides what happened, and she has never once volunteered the answer first.
answers.standout_quality: Seka finds herself alone at burnt places and says nothing about them until someone else notices, by which time the silence has already made her complicit in whatever happened there.
answers.accomplishment: When the village constable came to the burnt way station asking what she had found, Seka told him the poacher was trapped there, and let him ask three times before she said she had done the trapping.
answers.challenge: The village trappers won't take her word on anything until someone else has already confirmed it first, and Seka has stopped trying to convince them otherwise.
answers.peace: When she strips the outer leaves from flowers brought in from the margins—the ones nobody else has named—and builds them into form in a shallow bowl, the village trappers' refusal to listen stops mattering because the arrangement either works or it doesn't, and she will know which before she speaks.
answers.fear: At the burnt way station three winters past, she held the poacher's gaze while he asked for water, and she turned away because no one had asked her first what she had found there, and now when someone attractive meets her eye across a room she cannot look away the same manner, even though she knows the cost of that kind of refusal.
answers.past: Seka trapped a poacher at the burnt way station three winters ago and left him there without water or word to anyone, and the village still does not know if he died or walked out.
answers.known_for: The trappers along the Closed Shell road know Seka found the way station burnt down three winters past and never told anyone until the village constable asked her directly, and she still hasn't said whether the poacher walked out or didn't.
answers.prized_possession: Seka keeps the poacher's water flask, a dented copper thing that caught the light wrong when she found it near the way station's burnt stones, and when Chikafusa asked her directly what she had brought back from that place, she handed it to him instead of speaking.
answers.group_history: When the party first sheltered at a burnt wayhouse on the Closed Shell road, Seka recognized the copper flask Akio pulled from the ash and could not meet his eyes until he asked her directly whose it had been.
answers.raised_by: Chikafusa taught her to read the land by listening to nothing, so now Seka brings burnt things to the village trappers' workshop and waits for them to notice what she has already named in silence.

mentor.name: Chikafusa
mentor.text: Chikafusa taught Seka to read the land by touch and smell when his hearing went, which meant learning to say nothing until the silence itself had spoken first—a habit that fit her so well she has never shaken it, even now that she stands apart from him.

answers.stress_reaction: She stops answering questions altogether and waits for someone else to speak first, which leaves her in rooms where the silence has already decided what happened before anyone admits to needing her.
answers.relationships:
Akio (Yobanjin) — Akio of the Yobanjin came to the burnt way station asking about the poacher, and when Seka handed him the copper flask instead of speaking, he sat down beside the ash and waited until she had to break the silence herself.
Mirumoto Ichibei (Dragon) — Mirumoto Ichibei asked her to trap something that had been killing livestock in the Dragon lands, and when she brought him the dead thing instead of explaining how she had done it, he paid her in silver and never asked her name.
